title: “Iron” road in apple: the pathway regulated by MPK6-2–ERF4–FIT module
content: Plants need iron (Fe) nutrient for their photosynthesis and respiration. Despite its high abundance in the earth's crust, Fe is bio-unavailable for plant uptake in alkaline soil, which accounts for about one-third of the world's arable land (Riaz and Guerinot 2021). This limited availability leads to Fe deficiency in plants and becomes a limiting factor for crop yield and quality (Briat et al. 2015). While Fe regulatory mechanisms governing its acquisition from calcareous soil have been well documented in model plants, they remain unexplored in fruit trees.
